title: CI that blocks unapproved public APIs
hook: A public method on a shared library is a promise. If CI does not see that promise as a file diff, someone will ship a breaking change inside a “tiny helper” PR.

sections.heading: Treat the public surface as reviewed text
sections.prose: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers (and similar tools) keep `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` and `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` next to the project. Every public type and member must be listed. A new `public` method that is not in those files produces a diagnostic (commonly RS0016). CI fails. The author must add a line — that line is the review artifact, the same way an OpenAPI diff is the artifact for an HTTP contract. `Shipped` is what you already released; `Unshipped` is what this branch intends to release. At ship time you move lines from Unshipped to Shipped. InternalsVisibleTo (this module) exists so tests do not force `public` just to compile.

snippets.label: Unapproved public surface vs friend tests
snippets.explanation: EvictLocalAsync can stay internal and tested via InternalsVisibleTo. GetAsync is the contract. CI, not memory, enforces that split.

sections.heading: Obsolete, Experimental, and analyzers together
sections.prose: `[Obsolete("…", error: true)]` stops callers compiling against a dead path. `[Experimental("MyLib.AuthPreview")]` (C# 12) makes use a warning unless the caller suppresses that diagnostic id — useful for an LTI token validator you are not ready to support. Neither replaces a public API file: an experimental public type is still public and still a trim/doc/binary contract. Analyzers packaged with your NuGet (Roslyn SDK guidance) teach consumers; public API files protect you from yourself. Code-style naming rules (identifier conventions) are orthogonal: they keep `IWorkerQueue` looking like .NET, they do not version your surface.

snippets.label: Fail the build on API drift
snippets.explanation: PrivateAssets keeps the analyzer off your consumers. TreatWarningsAsErrors plus the RS diagnostic is what makes GitHub Actions block the merge.

sections.heading: What reviewers should look at
sections.prose: In a PR that adds `public`, read the `.txt` diff first, then the implementation. Ask: is this member returning a DTO or a domain type (module 18)? Does it allocate `string` copies of a CSV row that Span could have avoided (module 17)? Is the name PascalCase and free of double underscores reserved for the compiler (identifier-names guidance)? If the change is “make it public so the test project compiles,” reject and add InternalsVisibleTo. High-concurrency attempt-submit code that accidentally exposes a `public static` mutable dictionary is not a style issue; it is an API incident waiting for two Lambdas.

interviewTakeaways: Public API text files are the reviewed contract; undeclared public members fail CI.
Keep tests on InternalsVisibleTo so you do not inflate the shipped surface.
Obsolete and Experimental communicate intent; they do not replace a baseline diff.
commonPitfalls: Checking in Unshipped.txt growth forever and never promoting to Shipped at release.
Referencing the analyzer without PrivateAssets, so every consumer gets your RS diagnostics.
Making types public to silence tests instead of declaring a friend assembly.

jsTsCorrelations.note: api-extractor and `.d.ts` rollups fail CI when exported types drift. PublicAPI.Shipped.txt is the C# analogue for binary public surface, not for ambient types.
